summary.text: Fred Wellman is the Democratic nominee for Missouri's 2nd District. A West Point graduate and Army helicopter pilot who served more than 20 years, he later founded a communications firm for veterans and served as a senior advisor and executive director of the Lincoln Project. He is campaigning on affordability, healthcare and retirement security.

paragraphs.text: Wellman grew up in Kirkwood, Missouri, and graduated from Kirkwood High School.
He graduated from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1987 and later earned a master's degree from Harvard's Kennedy School (2007).

Ballotpedia lists his Army service as 1987 to 2010, as a helicopter pilot and officer with multiple deployments to Iraq; he earned his Ranger tab and describes himself as a third-generation military veteran.
In announcing his campaign, Wellman said he spent 22 years in the Army.
After retiring from the Army, Wellman founded ScoutComms, a firm that he says invested in veterans and military families, and worked as an advocate and consultant.
During the COVID-19 pandemic, he helped lead a team of Special Operations medical veterans that built and ran a field hospital in New York City.
He later served as Senior Advisor and Executive Director of the Lincoln Project and hosts the "On Democracy" podcast on the MeidasTouch network.
Wellman lives in Wildwood, according to his Ballotpedia survey.
On August 4, 2026, he won the Democratic primary for Missouri's 2nd District with 45.8% of the vote, ahead of Joan VonDras (43.0%) and Timothy Bilash (11.1%).
